model_reported.name: conduire-experience-optimisation
model_reported.summary: Used the valid serial and row-parallel results to choose an explicit-SIMD follow-up that keeps the serial traversal and does not claim a measured gain.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: No architecture-specific instruction or thread-creating construct is used; this serial experiment stays within any caller thread budget.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: No version-specific API or intrinsic is introduced; the source already has an OpenMP context, and the controller will validate compilation.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared the supplied repeated baseline and candidate measurements, treated them as observations rather than proof of SIMD benefit, and left new performance evaluation to the controller.

memory_lessons.applicability: This SIMD-only follow-up should be compared with the serial r-k-c measurements; the row-parallel measurement is useful context but does not isolate SIMD.
memory_lessons.claim: The serial r-k-c program was valid on all six checked cases, with n=1024 samples 0.076063603, 0.076956635, and 0.076168533 seconds. A row-parallel r-k-c program was also valid, with mean 0.009476690818181815 seconds. These results motivate testing SIMD separately and do not establish its effect.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this serial SIMD variant on all official sizes and compare repeated native n=1024 timings against the serial r-k-c result.

proposal.hypothesis: An explicit OpenMP SIMD directive over the contiguous c dimension may improve the already measured serial r-k-c traversal by making vectorization across each B/C row more explicit. This keeps k ascending for each output element and uses no additional threads, isolating SIMD as a follow-up to the serial traversal result; the previous row-parallel result motivates separate thread experiments but does not establish a SIMD benefit. Clearing C first preserves overwrite behavior.

retained: Change the r-c-k dot-product loop to a row-wise r-k-c rank-1 update, traversing B and C rows contiguously.
Add an OpenMP SIMD directive to the innermost c loop while retaining ascending-k accumulation for each output element.
Zero the complete output before accumulation and retain a runtime-size fallback; do not create worker threads.
